rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md. OLD (04-08): "...This lets platforms discover the authorization server protecting the resource without relying on domain conventions and prepares the deployment for future delegated IdP scenarios where the AS may not live on the business domain." rows.requirement: The issuer value in discovered metadata MUST byte-for-byte match the AS issuer resolved in Discovery Step 1 (which may now be a different origin than the business domain, via protected-resource metadata); platforms MUST NOT normalize before comparison.

(per
[RFC 8414 §3.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414#section-3.3){ target="_blank" }).

rows.notes: [2026-08-25] REWORDED — flag for review: relocated docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md. OLD (04-08): "The issuer value in the discovered metadata MUST match the discovery base URI exactly (per RFC 8414 §3.3). ... the value must be a byte-for-byte match." where 'discovery base URI' was ALWAYS the business's own domain (a flat two-tier hierarchy). NEW (08-25): "The issuer value in the discovered metadata MUST byte-for-byte match the AS issuer selected in Step 1 (per RFC 8414 §3.3)." Discovery is now a 3-step pipeline: a new Step 1 resolves the AS issuer via RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, and that issuer MAY be hosted on a different origin than the business domain (defaulting to the business domain only when no protected-resource metadata is published). The comparison target for byte-for-byte matching therefore changed from 'always the business domain' to 'whatever Step 1 resolved,' a genuine scope broadening, not just a rename. RFC 8414 §3.3. Converted from needs-oauth 2026-07-03: the OAuth harness (checks/oauth_harness.py) drives the authorization-code+PKCE flow as the platform; graded in merchant_checks_04_08_oauth.py. Business half graded (metadata issuer == discovery base, byte-for-byte); the 'platforms MUST NOT normalize' half is platform-bound.

out (see [Provider Selection](#provider-selection)) rather than rejecting the

rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass). Open-vocabulary tolerance rule on the platform's config-parsing behavior; manual.

rows.requirement: For oauth2 providers, platforms MUST discover the authorization server metadata from auth_url using the same two-tier metadata hierarchy as Discovery Step 2 (RFC 8414 primary with section 3.1 path insertion, OIDC fallback on 404 only), treating auth_url as the issuer.
rows.quote:
For `oauth2` providers, platforms **MUST** discover the authorization server
metadata from `auth_url` using the same two-tier metadata hierarchy as
[Discovery](#discovery) Step 2 (RFC 8414 primary with §3.1 path insertion,
OIDC fallback on 404 only), treating `auth_url` as the issuer. The
protected-resource step does not apply — `auth_url` is already the IdP
issuer — and the business validates the JWT grant's `iss` against it per
[Business Token Issuance](#business-token-issuance).
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass). Platform-side IdP-metadata discovery procedure; manual.

rows.requirement: For the chaining path, config.providers is a closed allowlist: a business MUST reject a JWT authorization grant whose iss does not match a listed oauth2 mechanism entry.
rows.quote:
for the chaining path, it is a closed
allowlist — a business **MUST** reject a JWT authorization grant
whose `iss` does not match a listed `oauth2` mechanism entry (see
[Business Token Issuance](#business-token-issuance)).
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass): the allowlist-closure guarantee underlying the whole Accelerated IdP Flow's trust model. Needs-oauth: proving rejection requires presenting a live JWT grant with an unlisted iss.

rows.requirement: Platforms requesting a JWT authorization grant via token exchange MUST include at least one of resource/audience (the business's AS issuer URI); when both are sent to the IdP they MUST carry identical values in the resulting grant's aud claim.
rows.quote:
`resource` and/or `audience`: the business's authorization server
      issuer URI. Platforms **MUST** include at least one.
      [RFC 8693 §2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8693#section-2.1){ target="_blank" }
      permits URI values in either parameter; IdP implementations vary
      in which they accept. The IdP maps the value to the `aud` claim
      in the resulting grant; when both are sent they **MUST** carry
      identical values.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass): the token-exchange request parameters step of the Accelerated IdP Flow. The IdP Requirements section restates the identical-values half at L687-689 (see WAIVERS-PROPOSED.md — covered directly by IDL-073's quote span rather than waived separately). Needs-oauth: verifying the issued grant's aud claim requires a live token-exchange call.

rows.requirement: The platform MUST NOT present a raw IdP token directly to a business.
rows.quote:
The platform **MUST NOT** present a raw IdP token directly to a business.
Identity chaining ensures each business issues tokens under its own authority
with the correct audience binding and scope policy.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass). Core Accelerated IdP Flow security invariant; platform-bound send-behavior, manual (matches the IDL-002/003/004 platform-request-shape precedent).

rows.requirement: The JWT authorization grant MUST conform to RFC 7523 section 3, with two UCP-specific constraints: aud MUST be a single value (the business's AS issuer URI), not an array, and jti MUST be present (RFC 7523 only says MAY) so businesses can enforce single-use replay protection.
rows.quote:
The grant **MUST** conform to
[RFC 7523 §3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-3){ target="_blank" },
with two UCP-specific constraints:

* `aud` **MUST** be a single value (the business's AS issuer URI), not an
  array — chaining targets one business per grant.
* `jti` **MUST** be present (RFC 7523 says MAY) so businesses can enforce
  single-use replay protection (see [Security Considerations](#security-considerations)).
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass): the core replay-protection constraint on the JWT authorization grant itself (jti presence tightens the base RFC's MAY to a UCP MUST). One of the more consequential new MUSTs in this section. The earlier preview sentence at L523-524 ('aud MUST be a single-valued URI plus a unique jti') restates this — see WAIVERS-PROPOSED.md, duplicate_of IDL-074. Needs-oauth: verifying aud/jti on an issued grant requires a live token-exchange call.

rows.requirement: Upon receiving a JWT authorization grant, the business's authorization server MUST validate the assertion per RFC 7523 section 3, with UCP-specific requirements: iss MUST match the auth_url of a listed oauth2 mechanism entry; aud MUST match the business's own AS issuer URI exactly; the JWT signature MUST be verified against the IdP's jwks_uri, and the business MUST fail closed if the JWKS cannot be retrieved.
rows.quote:
business's authorization server **MUST** validate the assertion per
[RFC 7523 §3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-3){ target="_blank" },
with the following UCP-specific requirements:

* `iss` **MUST** match the `auth_url` of an `oauth2` mechanism entry
  listed in `config.providers`.
* `aud` **MUST** match the business's own AS issuer URI exactly.
* The JWT signature **MUST** be verified against the IdP's `jwks_uri`; if
  JWKS cannot be retrieved, the business **MUST** fail closed.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass): the business-side grant-validation contract (iss allowlist match, exact aud match, signature verification, fail-closed on JWKS unavailability). Needs-oauth: testing requires presenting live grants (valid and deliberately invalid) to the business's token endpoint.

rows.requirement: If no requested scope can be satisfied by an Accelerated-IdP-Flow grant's claims, the business MUST return invalid_scope per RFC 6749 section 5.2.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass). Distinct error-handling obligation from IDL-075 (post-validation scope-satisfaction failure, not grant-validity failure). Needs-oauth.

rows.requirement: If user interaction (terms acceptance, onboarding) is required, the business MUST reject the JWT authorization grant with invalid_grant.
rows.quote:
If user interaction is required (terms acceptance,
onboarding), the business **MUST** reject the grant with `invalid_grant`
(see [Chaining Errors at the Token Endpoint](#chaining-errors-at-the-token-endpoint))
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass). Distinct trigger from IDL-076 and IDL-078 (interactive-onboarding-required case). Needs-oauth.

rows.requirement: When the JWT authorization grant lacks a claim the business requires for account resolution, the business MUST reject with invalid_grant.
rows.quote:
**Missing or insufficient claims.** When the JWT authorization grant
lacks a claim the business requires (e.g., `email` for account
resolution), the business **MUST** reject with `invalid_grant`.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass). Distinct trigger from IDL-077 (missing-claim case, not interaction-required case). Needs-oauth.

rows.requirement: Identity providers of type oauth2 listed in config.providers MUST publish authorization server metadata via RFC 8414 or OpenID Connect Discovery, and that metadata MUST include revocation_endpoint, jwks_uri, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange in grant_types_supported.
rows.quote:
Identity providers of `type: oauth2` listed in `config.providers` **MUST**
publish authorization server metadata via
[RFC 8414](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414){ target="_blank" }
or OpenID Connect Discovery. The metadata **MUST** include:

* `revocation_endpoint` — to support token revocation per the
    [Token Lifecycle](#token-lifecycle) section.
* `jwks_uri` — so businesses can verify the signature on JWT authorization
    grants issued by the IdP.
* `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` in `grant_types_supported`
    — to enable the Accelerated IdP Flow.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass): IdP-side metadata publication requirement, analogous to IDL-016/017's business-side RFC 8414 metadata rows. Testable: metadata is fetchable and its field presence directly checkable, no live grant needed.

rows.requirement: When processing token exchange requests for JWT authorization grants, the IdP MUST authenticate the platform and verify it is authorized to present the subject token; MUST verify the target business is a known relying party the user has authorized (resource/audience MUST carry identical values when both are sent) and MUST NOT issue grants for businesses the user has not authorized; MUST issue a grant conforming to the JWT Authorization Grant requirements; and MUST return issued_token_type as the jwt token-type URN.
rows.quote:
When processing token exchange requests for JWT authorization grants, the
IdP **MUST**:

* Authenticate the platform and verify it is authorized to present the
    subject token
    ([RFC 8693 §2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8693#section-2.1){ target="_blank" }).
* Verify the target business (identified by `resource` and/or `audience`,
    which **MUST** carry identical values when both are sent — see
    [Flow](#flow)) is a known relying party and the user has authorized
    identity sharing with it. The IdP **MUST NOT** issue grants for
    businesses the user has not authorized.
* Issue a JWT authorization grant conforming to the
    [JWT Authorization Grant](#jwt-authorization-grant) requirements.
* Return `issued_token_type` as `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt`.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass): the IdP's own token-exchange obligations (the counterpart actor to IDL-072/IDL-074, not a business or platform). Bundles all four bullets, including the resource/audience identical-values restatement (see IDL-072) and the not-issue-unauthorized-grants MUST NOT, into one row. Needs-oauth: requires a live token-exchange call to the IdP.

rows.requirement: Advertised scopes MUST apply uniformly across identity paths: the same config.scopes map governs availability whether the platform obtained identity via direct OAuth or the Accelerated IdP Flow, and a business honoring min_acr (for example) MUST apply the same threshold regardless of path.
rows.quote:
Advertised scopes **MUST** apply uniformly across identity paths. The
same `config.scopes` map governs scope availability whether the platform
obtained user identity via direct OAuth or the
[Accelerated IdP Flow](#accelerated-idp-flow). Per-scope policy gates
which assertions satisfy a scope; businesses honoring `min_acr` (for
example) **MUST** apply the same threshold regardless of path.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass): the cross-path scope-consistency guarantee that keeps the Accelerated IdP Flow from becoming a lower-assurance side door around config.scopes policy. Needs-oauth: verifying uniformity requires exercising both identity paths and comparing outcomes.

rows.requirement: JWT authorization grants MUST be short-lived.
rows.quote:
**JWT grant lifetime.** JWT authorization grants **MUST** be short-lived;
the `exp` claim **SHOULD** be no more than 60 seconds after `iat`.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass). A qualitative restatement (the only concrete threshold is a SHOULD, not this MUST); no hard testable bound, hence manual rather than needs-oauth/testable.

rows.requirement: Businesses MUST enforce single-use JWT authorization grants by tracking the jti claim within the grant's validity window.
rows.quote:
**JWT grant single-use.** Businesses **MUST** enforce single-use JWT;
a short exp narrows the replay window, but only jti tracking closes it.
authorization grants by tracking the `jti` claim within the grant's
validity window.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass): the runtime replay-tracking enforcement duty, distinct from IDL-074's jti-presence field requirement. Note: the source prose itself reads as if an editorial sentence ('a short exp narrows the replay window, but only jti tracking closes it.') was inserted mid-sentence, breaking grammatical continuity between 'enforce single-use JWT' and 'authorization grants by tracking the jti claim' — quoted verbatim as vendored; the core MUST is unambiguous regardless. Needs-oauth: proving enforcement requires replaying a used grant and observing rejection.

rows.requirement: Businesses MUST NOT store or forward JWT authorization grants received from platforms.
rows.quote:
**Grant relay.** Businesses **MUST NOT** store or forward JWT
authorization grants received from platforms. Grants are bearer
credentials scoped to a single audience (`aud`) and a single use.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b pass). A data-handling/retention restriction on the business's internal storage, not observable via a single API probe; manual.

rows.requirement: To prevent Mix-Up Attacks, Businesses MUST return iss in every authorization response (paired with the Platform's RFC 9207 iss validation) -- without iss validation, an attacker controlling one authorization server can redirect a victim's authorization code to a different server.
rows.quote:
* **Mix-Up Attack prevention.** Platforms **MUST** validate the `iss`
  parameter in the authorization response
  ([RFC 9207](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9207){ target="_blank" }).
  Businesses **MUST**
  return `iss` in every authorization response. Without `iss` validation,
  an attacker that controls one authorization server can redirect a
rows.notes: New row, 2026-08-25 census closure wave (Mix-Up Attack prevention, business-side iss echo).

notes: No official conformance oracle exists for identity-linking: .vendor/conformance contains only checkout/order/fulfillment/card-credential/webhook/etc. tests; grep found no identity-linking, oauth, or scope tests. All rows official_oracle=false.

2026-08-25 is the doc-reorg + provider-chaining release: docs/specification/identity-linking.md -> docs/specification/common/identity-linking/index.md (#723 hierarchy reorg). The identity-linking capability grew substantially: config.providers (a 'reserved extension point' in 04-08) is now a REAL, shipped feature (a new 'provider' $def in the schema, plus new doc sections Identity Providers / Accelerated IdP Flow / IdP Requirements) enabling JWT-bearer-assertion identity chaining (RFC 8693 token exchange + RFC 7523 JWT bearer grant) so platforms can skip the browser-based OAuth flow with a trusted upstream IdP. Discovery also gained a new leading step (RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata resolves the AS issuer, which MAY now be a different origin than the business domain) ahead of the previously-only two-tier RFC 8414/OIDC hierarchy. These are the two structural deltas driving this version's reworded rows (IDL-001, IDL-030, IDL-033, IDL-056, IDL-057, IDL-059, IDL-062). No row was found DEAD in 08-25.

Identity linking EXISTED in the 2026-01-23 version, but the 2026-04-08 version REWORKED it onto capability-driven scopes ({capability}:{scope}) and RFC 8414 authorization-server discovery. This is the spec-significant delta; flagged on rows IDL-001, IDL-016, IDL-029, IDL-037, IDL-059 in the 04-08 register.

Almost all normative rows are OAuth-flow obligations requiring a live authorization server / browser-driven consent, hence testability=needs-oauth or manual. The fetch-only obligations (RFC 8414 metadata presence: scopes_supported, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported, code_challenge_methods_supported, authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported, protected-resource metadata, well-known publication) are marked testable. TLS-1.2-minimum (IDL-053) is testable but not browser_capable (transport-level inspection).

schema_enforced=true only for real JSON-Schema constraints in identity_linking.json: scope_token regex pattern (IDL-037/IDL-059) and the required config/scopes structure (IDL-060). The scope-name pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ in prose (IDL-037) is a subset of the full schema scope_token pattern, which itself was BROADENED in 08-25 to allow hyphens (IDL-059, reworded).

Scope vocabulary referenced across rows: *.catalog.*:read, dev.ucp.shopping.checkout:manage, dev.ucp.shopping.order:read, dev.ucp.shopping.order:manage (well-known); businesses MAY declare custom scopes following the same {capability}:{scope} convention.

config.scopes (UCP hard gates: scopes that REQUIRE user auth) vs OAuth scopes_supported (accepted vocabulary the AS will honor) are distinct; their set difference is the optional/auth-unlocked layer (IDL-017, IDL-038, IDL-054).

Schema reorg note (source/schemas/common/identity_linking.json): the scope_policy.description $ref changed from '../shopping/types/description.json' to 'types/description.json' (a common/types/ relocation, per the harness-provided reorg map) — no existing row quotes that $ref, so no row was affected. The schema's top-level and config-level $comment fields (describing config.providers as a future reserved extension point) were REMOVED, consistent with providers now being a real, documented property.

P2b addition (2026-08-30): 22 new rows (IDL-063..IDL-084) extracting the Accelerated IdP Flow / config.providers mechanics that the register-completeness census proved unregistered (49 missed MUST/MUST NOT occurrences in this file; 12 of the 49 were duplicate-of-existing-row restatements or quote-fragment/line-wrap boundary artifacts of IDL-012/IDL-017/IDL-020/IDL-026/IDL-030/IDL-050/IDL-051/IDL-065/IDL-074, proposed as waivers in WAIVERS-PROPOSED.md rather than new rows; the remaining 37 cover genuinely new normative surface with no 04-08 antecedent, since the Accelerated IdP Flow itself did not exist before this version). No existing IDL-001..062 row was modified.
